newsitem.title: USA: Mexico's Zedillo pledges growth with human face.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo pledges growth with human face.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Wednesday pledged to use his powers to create sustained economic growth with a "human face" in his country and said his administration was committed to democracy.

"I will use my powers to create sustained economic growth," Zedillo told an audience of Mexican-Americans. "But wealth with a human face. A human face for the millions who want a just wage," a good education and human rights.
"Mexico has proven you can have democracy with sustained economic growth," he added, noting Mexico's economic expansion was continuing this year after last year's 5 percent growth.

"I am confident that all political parties will meet the challenges of the new pluralism," he said, praising the effort that went into making elections held earlier this month in Mexico free and fair.
Two opposition parties made large gains against his ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which has maintained an uninterrupted grip on power for 68 years.
Zedillo said in a recent interview with the Chicago Tribune that the PRI was not guaranteed the presidency when elections are held in 2000.

"We, the people of Mexico, are more united than ever before in taking the definite step toward democracy," he told the annual convention of the National Council of La Raza, a Mexican-American business and charitable group.

Zedillo said Mexico was committed to free trade, and praised the 4-year-old North American Free Trade Agreement which he said had increased bilateral trade with the United States by 70 percent, "far beyond the most optimistic predictions." He said safeguarding the environment would not be sacrificed in the drive to increase trade.
Zedillo also decried last weekend's discovery of deaf-mute Mexican immigrants living in squalid conditions in New York City who were deployed to beg on the city's subways.
Calling the New York discoveries "atrocities," he promised severe punishments for anyone caught smuggling immigrants with disabilities into the United States from Mexico.
"We are working hard to create the opportunities that our countrymen come looking for here," he said.
